newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 21.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - April 21.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi Tel:3324842, 3351006, 3761233 Fax:+91-11-3351006 Internet: biznis@giasbm01.vsnl.net.in
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
TOP STORIES
The Times Of India
INDER KUMAR GUJRAL IS NEXT PRIME MINISTER

After a day-long suspense over the formation of the next government, President Shankar Dayal Sharma appointed I.K. Gujral as the next prime minister. He was asked to prove his majority in the lower house on April 22. Gujral will announce his cabinet after winning the vote of confidence. Indications were that initially only members of parties forming the ruling coalition would be included in the cabinet. However, the chances of the Congress joining the government at a later stage could not be ruled out, sources said.
The Economic Times
EXPORT POLICY TO BEAT THE SLUMP ON THE CARDS

Following a dismal export performance in 1996/97 (April-March), the Commerce Ministry was working out a long-term and short-term policy to tackle such slumps in the future. Commerce ministry officials said that in the long term the ministry was in favour of India becoming a major player in exporting of commodities which were growing and not in commodities where world demands remained stagnant.
CAR SALES PEAK TO 400,000 BUT BUMPS EXPECTED

Car sales for 1996/97 (April-March) touched a record 400,000, up from 345,000. The automobile sector, especially the car segment, was one of the few areas which attracted the highest foreign direct investment. But almost 95 percent of the proposed $2 billion-odd investment was directed at the mid-size and upmarket segment where the market was still at a nascent stage.
EIGHT PCT GROWTH TARGET SET FOR NEW GOVERNMENT

The leading industry body, CII, set an eight percent GDP growth rate target to be achieved by the government in the current fiscal. It, however, cautioned that a lot depended on how the grey areas were tackled. In its background paper, the CII ackowledged that the change in policy environment since 1991 was one of the major factors propelling growth rate.
TYRE IMPORTS TO HIT CAR RADIAL MAKERS

Radial tyre manufacturers were expected to face tough competition following the government's decision to put the import of all kinds of tyres under the open general licence (OGL). This, industry experts said, would lead to cheaper international radial tyre brands flooding local markets.
Financial Express
BUDGET TO SAIL THROUGH

The possible exit of Finance Minister P. Chidambaram was unlikely to pose any problems for the passage of the budget in the special parliamentary session beginning Monday. Though the minister said the fate of the budget would be decided by the incoming government, sources in the ruling United Front pointed out it was unlikely I.K. Gujral, the new leader, would allow any changes in the budget. Gujral has already said he would continue the economic policies of the previous government, hinting at the commitment of his government to honour the budget in its current shape.
PEPSICO EXPECTS TO BREAK EVEN THIS YEAR

Pepsico's India operation is expected to reach the break-even stage this year with the cola giant setting a combined turnover target of over 12 billion rupees for 1997 from its two main ventures. Sources said the company's bottling operations under Pepsico India Holdings alone hoped to achieve a seven billion rupee sales income. Pepsi Foods hopes to post a turnover of five billion rupees in the calendar year.
